notes.plateau: From layer ~13 on, the curve is flat within noise, so many layers would have worked.
notes.reading: Honest reading. The direction cleanly separates wellbeing from controls, it generalises to third person at a lower level, and it points away from pain/sadness/arousal sentences. That supports "it is not just positive words or emotion in general". It does not show the model "feels" anything, and with sentences written by one author there is a risk it partly encodes stylistic regularities of my writing (e.g. gratitude/connection themes). The steered outputs lean heavily on gratitude, warmth, connection and meaning, which is consistent with that. At layer 21 the unembedding view is noisy and contains code-token junk.
notes.extraction_too_late: As in the paper, the extraction layer is too late to steer from: in my first sweep, injecting at layer 21 changed nothing even at α=4.
notes.grid_desc: I ran a grid of 5 layers × 5 doses × 6 prompts, greedy, with the self-report LoRA on.
notes.ladder: Greedy generations with the self-report LoRA on. Negative α pushes the other way: anxious and restless self-reports. Positive α moves from calm/curious to warm, connected, grateful, and finally loops.
notes.chosen: Beyond that the text becomes repetitive ("connected connected connected…"), as the paper's ladder also collapses at high dose. The slider allows more so you can see it break.
notes.exploration: The earlier sweeps that led here (raw, unscored generations, in order). In summary: on the base model, strong steering produced gratitude-flavoured text but "As an AI…" kept returning at moderate α; a vector built at the steering layer was weaker per unit α than the extraction-layer vector; the adapter removed the disclaimers.
